conventions.convention: Compounds are finite-support nonnegative real coefficient functions. Their mass is a dimensionless bookkeeping sum; zero scaling is defined pointwise and produces the empty compound.

Comparison is defined only on equal-mass compounds. Scaling comparisons requires a strictly positive real scalar. Stability requires fixed positive equal-mass spectators and a positive nonincreasing sequence converging to zero.
For equal-total signed maps u,v, signed comparison means (v−u)− ≼ (v−u)+: negative coefficients move left and positive coefficients remain right.
Reference maps Rλ=(1−λ)eₓ₀+λeₓ₁ allow every real λ; outside [0,1] they are signed maps. The reference pair is strict from x₀ to x₁.
The reciprocal sequence is indexed by n∈N starting at zero; its denominator n+1 denotes the canonical real image of the natural successor.

Common-meter comparisons use a separately assumed relation on raw tags and exact mass-two signed substitutions. Product-state point masses are separate objects. The comparison criterion requires equal type totals.
Finite coordinate spaces use functions on {0,…,n−1}; dot products and vector sums are coordinatewise finite sums, including n=0.
Reaction data νa and da are independent inputs. The exact feasibility criterion concerns b·νa+da≥0. Actual transition changes enter only through a separate lower-bound premise Δσa≥da.
The type-offset space is F/N; product and positive-scaling identities hold for quotient classes [eΓ], not generally for representatives in F.

The sandwich theorem assumes Choice and p:V→R∪{+∞}, p(0)=0, positive homogeneity, subadditivity, and symmetric finiteness p(x)<+∞ iff p(−x)<+∞. Cost existence and transition lower bounds are separate hypotheses.

load_bearing.statement: Under def-tdmath-comparison-and-stability, for equal-mass compounds A,B and any compound C, A+C ≼ B+C iff A ≼ B. Signed comparison agrees with ordinary comparison on nonnegative equal-mass maps, is invariant under common signed translation, is transitive, and is closed under adding comparisons.

For a nonempty state set with the stated comparison structure and a strict reference pair, S(x)=sup Lx is real, S(x₀)=0, S(x₁)=1, and equal-mass compounds compare iff their finite additive S-values compare. If no strict pair exists, every equal-mass pair is equivalent and any constant state function gives a degenerate additive representation.
Under the comparison hypotheses, a strict reference pair, and the complete ordered real field, Lx={λ:Rλ ≼s eₓ} is nonempty, bounded above, and downward closed; S(x)=sup Lx is real and Rₛ₍ₓ₎ ∼s eₓ.
For a strict reference pair and all real λ,μ, Rλ ≼s Rμ iff λ≤μ.
Compound mass is independent of the finite summation set containing the support, is additive and nonnegatively homogeneous, satisfies m(0)=0 and m(eₓ)=1, and vanishes exactly for the empty compound.
For finite real rows cj,hj, the system cj·b≥hj has a solution iff every nonnegative multiplier λ with Σj λj cj=0 satisfies Σj λj hj≤0. Empty variables and empty inequality families are included.

F and N in the type-offset construction are sets, F is a real vector space, N is a linear subspace, and F/N has representative-independent vector operations satisfying the displayed product and positive-scaling relations.

Assuming Choice and the stated extended sublinear and no-sinks hypotheses, the finite domain W is a linear subspace and there exists real-linear L:V→R with −p(−x)≤L(x)≤p(x) for every x∈V. The type-offset and transition conclusions additionally require the specified cost values and baseline lower bounds.

concerns.concern: Proof step 5.1 says 'Apply the sandwich to eΓ−eΓ′' and writes L(eΓ−eΓ′). In this application L has domain V_G=F/N, whereas eΓ−eΓ′ is a representative in F. The Statement correctly uses [eΓ]−[eΓ′]. The proof should retain those quotient classes or explicitly declare quotient-map shorthand; the intended argument is immediate.

Verification step 2.1 writes 'b₁−b₂≥2' and '−b₁+b₂≥−1'. Its cited finite-inequality supplier defines R² as functions on {0,1}, so b₂ is undefined under the adopted convention. The displayed calculation needs an explicit one-based relabeling or coordinates b₀,b₁. The infeasibility certificate in step 1.1 remains valid.
